description:
FILED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7), as the measured residue of #550 (the
`%` whole-container repair) and #449 (the CL-unsafe `@` names).  Every row
below was probed one character at a time, `@X = (1,2); scalar(@X)` and
`%X = (a=>1); keys %X`, against perl 5.40.3.  ALL PRE-EXISTING; none is a
regression of s449s.

STATE AFTER s449s (the matrix, 29 punctuation characters):
  ARRAY container works for  ! % & * . / < = > ? ^ _ ~ , | @ \  (17)
  HASH  container works for  % & , . < = > ? ^ _ | ~            (12; `!` `+` `-`
                             are perl-READ-ONLY, see below)

THE RESIDUE, by cause -- the causes are DIFFERENT and should not be folded:

(a) THE TOKEN SWALLOWED THE LINE.  `@"`, `@'`, "@`" and `@#` (and the `%`
    twins) -- PPI builds a Quote::Double / Quote::Single / QuoteLike::Backtick
    / comment out of the character and everything after it, so the name cannot
    be recovered from the token stream at all.  A repair would have to work on
    the SOURCE before tokenizing, the way `_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` does
    for a derailed diamond (#563).  Note `@'` is doubly special: `'` is perl's
    OLD PACKAGE SEPARATOR, so `@'foo` is `@main::foo` and only a BARE `@'` is
    the array named `'`.

(b) THE NAME IS A Token::Structure.  `@(`, `@)`, `@[`, `@]`, `@;` (and the `%`
    twins) -- PPI hands the character over as a Structure the LEXER has already
    built a Structure node around, so consuming it means deleting a bracket
    that has a partner.  `_repair_punct_glob_name` has an arm for exactly this
    (`*]`) and its discriminator is PPI's own: an orphan closer is parked in a
    PPI::Statement::UnmatchedBrace.  That test is the starting point.

(c) `%/` DERAILS INTO A REGEXP.  `Operator(%) Regexp::Match(/;…)` -- the same
    §14 cascade family as #563, one sigil over.

(d) `%@` AND `%\` REACH THE REPAIR BUT NOT THE TARGET.  The `%` repair rewrites
    into perl's block spelling `%{X}` (strict-safe, unlike `%{'X'}`), and PCL
    DROPS `%{@}` and `%{\}` -- inside the block PPI makes a sigil character a
    Cast with nothing to cast, and PCL's `${PUNCTUATION}` fold (§9) has no case
    for it.  The `@` twins `@@` and `@\` DO work, because that repair splices a
    Symbol node instead of rewriting text.  So this one is a PCL gap in the
    §9 fold, not a PPI bug.

(e) `@:` AND `%:` ARE A CL READ ERROR -- the worst failure mode in the family,
    because it kills the WHOLE FILE at load rather than one statement:

      no strict; @: = (1,2); print scalar(@:), "\n";
      perl: 2
      PCL : read error during load -- the emitted `(p-array-= @: …)` has a
            BARE `@:`, and `:` is CL's package marker

    PPI lexes `@:` as a Symbol already, so no repair is involved: it is purely
    the emission spelling.  `Pl::CLForm::needs_pipes` deliberately does NOT
    have `:` in its CL-unsafe set, because `cl_sym`'s callers pass qualified
    names (`Foo::bar`) that must keep their package marker -- so the fix is at
    the site that spells a punctuation VARIABLE, not in the shared predicate.

(f) `$x %$y` IS A DEREF IN PERL, MODULO IN PCL (silent wrong):

      my $x = 17; my $y = \5; print "3=", $x %$y, "\n";
      perl: 3=17     -- `%$y` is a HASH DEREF; perl prints $x then the (empty) hash
      PCL : 3=0      -- modulo of a reference

    perl's toke.c decides `%` before `$`/`{`/an identifier by SPACING, not by
    the term/operator position #550's repair uses.  Out of #550's scope (that
    repair only ever looks at a PUNCTUATION character after the `%`), and it
    needs its own probe set: `$x % $y`, `$x %$y`, `$x %{$y}`, `$x % $y` with
    tabs, and the `@` sibling `$x @$y` (a syntax error, so principle 9 applies).

(g) ASSIGNING TO A READ-ONLY MAGIC CONTAINER.  perl refuses `%! = (…)`
    ("ERRNO hash is read-only"), `@+ = (…)` and `@- = (…)` ("Modification of a
    read-only value attempted"); PCL performs the assignment.  Pre-existing and
    a different family (magic containers), listed here only because the matrix
    shows it.

BAR: whichever cause is taken, the full 29-character matrix vs perl before and
after (the probe is `punctmatrix.pl`, trivially rewritten from this
description), the modulo negatives from Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t, and
corpus-diff + emission-ab (the s449s widening of `needs_pipes` moved exactly 3
files of 921 -- `t/comp/package.t` and two Text-CSV eol tests -- so the
population is sensitive to this area).

(h) THE INTERPOLATED SUBSCRIPT of the newly-working names is a SILENT WRONG.
    `Pl::InterpScan`'s $PUNCT_ARRAY_SUBSCRIPT set (task #451) held the
    CL-unsafe characters out for exactly the #449 reason, and that reason is
    gone -- but the set is the SUBSCRIPT question, not the spelling question,
    so each character needs its own probe (that is #451's own ruling: `^` is in
    one set and not the other).  Measured s449s, `@X = (11,22,33); print
    "$X[1]"`:

        char   perl   PCL
         ,      22    the literal `[1]`
         |      22    `0[1]`
         @      22    the literal `[1]`
         \      22    the literal `[1]`
         ?      22    22            (already in the set, shown as the control)

    `\` needs the escape rule thought through before it is added: this scanner
    hides the character after a backslash from reference detection, while perl
    consumes the `\` into the variable NAME first.
subject: The punctuation-container residue after #550/#449: the quote-swallowing names, the Structure-named ones, `%/`, `%@`/`%\`, `@:`/`%:` (a CL READ ERROR), and `$x %$y` (a deref in perl, modulo in PCL)
